title: Determine the exact odd denominator of the canonical width-13 Clifford decoder
body:
At width 13, the canonical Moore–Penrose decoder for the full four-qubit Clifford alphabet has least common odd denominator **22,742,436,009,630,709,072,767,882,717,680,300,149,753,125**. This answers the canonical-denominator question left in #7802, where another norm-optimal left inverse required only 470,624,175.

The dyadic splitting transfers the question to the inverse Gram matrix. The 81 character blocks give an upper bound. Its diagonal entry supplies every required odd factor except one power of three. The off-diagonal entry at the explicit order-17 Clifford of #6208 supplies that power. Their denominator least common multiple meets the upper bound.

Two independent programs compute the spectrum and check that witness. All four registered commands passed under CPython 3.12.14 in the checkout and in a read-only Git-free export. The committed bytes, source history, file modes and exported input inventory passed the repository checks. The result concerns exact coefficient denominators; a priced division circuit remains open.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-canonical-denominator
```

Ali Romman supplied #7772, #7788 and #7792, and Nick Petalas supplied the #7747 projection. The argument also uses the splitting in #7799 and the distinction between minimizers in #7802. Prepared by apoursh with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. The selected conditional multiplication exponent is unaffected. [Proof at the submitted revision](https://github.com/apoursh/integer-mult-bounds/blob/d3df403a13bee082a8cef62f190024aaf0cd08dd/research/clifford-canonical-denominator/PROOF.md) · [Research claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19754792)
